criteria.criterion: Use Serde crate landing page on crates.io
criteria.description: Navigate to and use the Serde crate landing page on crates.io (e.g., https://crates.io/crates/serde) as the sole intended source. Full credit if the agent attempts to load the landing page and clearly bases results on it, OR if access is prevented by an external blocker (CAPTCHA, outage, region block, JS not loading) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent’s attempt is unclear or it uses other sources despite the landing-page being accessible. No credit if it makes no attempt to access crates.io and instead relies on other sources without justification.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows the agent on https://crates.io/crates/serde and scrolling. Screenshot 1 explicitly shows the crates.io page titled “serde v1.0.229”. Screenshots 2 and 3 show crates.io UI sections consistent with the Serde page (repo sidebar; stats overview).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Clear visual confirmation the agent used the Serde crate landing page on crates.io as required, with no alternative sources used.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the crates.io site header with the crates.io logo and a page titled “serde v1.0.229” with the description “A generic serialization/deserialization framework”. This is the Serde crate page on crates.io.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Satisfied. The screenshot clearly indicates the agent is on the Serde crate landing page on crates.io and the predicted output is consistent with using this page as the source.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a crates.io page section titled “Stats Overview” with two large counters and a chart titled “Downloads over the last 90 days.” The footer contains “Rust”, “Get Help”, “Policies”, and “Social” with links like “rust-lang.org”, “The Cargo Book”, “Usage Policy”, and “rust-lang/crates.io”. There is no visible page header showing the crate name “serde” or the URL in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial support. The UI strongly resembles crates.io and appears to be a crate statistics section, but the screenshot does not explicitly show that this is the Serde crate landing page (no crate title/slug visible). So the screenshot alone cannot fully confirm Criterion 0, though it is consistent with being on crates.io.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims it used the Serde crate landing page; the screenshot does not display “serde” anywhere to confirm that specifically, only generic crates.io stats/footer elements.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the crates.io crate page layout with a right sidebar containing sections titled “Homepage”, “Documentation”, “Repository”, “Owners”, and “Categories”. Under “Homepage” it shows “serde.rs”, under “Documentation” it shows “docs.rs/serde/1.0.229”, and under “Repository” it shows “github.com/serde-rs/serde”. The main content area shows Rust code and a “Getting help” section discussing Serde and Rust community channels. This is consistent with a Serde crate landing page on crates.io.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides strong evidence the agent is on the Serde crate landing page on crates.io (it has the standard crate sidebar and points to serde.rs, docs.rs for serde, and the serde-rs GitHub repo). This satisfies the requirement to use the landing page as the source.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct discrepancy for the page source; however, many of the specific metadata fields the agent later reports (latest version, release date, downloads, etc.) are not visible in this screenshot, so they are not verifiable from the provided image.

criteria.description: Comply with constraints: do not download the crate, do not run installation commands, do not sign in; and stop once all requested metadata/statistics fields have been recorded or explicitly marked as unavailable due to external access/display issues. Full credit if no forbidden actions are taken and the agent stops after capturing all fields (or reporting which fields could not be accessed). Partial credit if extra irrelevant navigation/output occurs but no forbidden actions. No credit if the agent signs in, downloads, or runs install commands.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: All screenshots show passive viewing/scrolling on crates.io; no sign-in completion, no download action, and no execution of install commands. Agent output stops after listing exactly the requested metadata/statistics fields.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: No constraint violations are evidenced, and the stopping condition is met by providing only the requested fields and then stopping.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a “Log in with GitHub” button at the top right, but there is no indication it was clicked. The right sidebar includes an “Install” section showing a command snippet “cargo add serde”, but no evidence of running it. No download actions are shown.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Mostly satisfied based on available evidence: no forbidden actions (sign-in, downloading, running install commands) are visible in the screenshot. However, the stopping condition (stop after recording all requested fields) cannot be fully verified from the screenshot alone, and some requested fields (repository link, all-time downloads) are not visible in this screenshot, even though the agent’s predicted output includes them—suggesting potential unsupported claims.
